articleTitle: Improving distribution network resilience against earthquakes
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Historically, reliability analysis has ignored the occurrence of natural hazards such as those associated with extreme weather, flooding, earthquakes and tsunamis, which are becoming more and more relevant due to recent events. In this content, we present an assessment methodology to determine the resiliency levels of a distribution system e,posed to a major earthquake. The proposed 4-stage methodology models (i) the earthquake, (ii) the fragility of network components, (iv) the network outages, and (v) the impacts on network operation (including the energy not supplied) through sequential Monte Carlo simulations. This methodology is used to study the resilience of distribution networks under two particular strategies: one that hardens substations infrastructure in order to reduce their fragility levels, and the other one that uses additional network infrastructure in the form of transfer cables to shift load among substations in case a major event occurs. Through several case studies based on a real distribution network in Chile, we demonstrate that hardening substations infrastructure may be a more resilient way to deal with earthquakes, even when compared to an alternative, extreme case where a vast number of transfer cables are installed to support damaged substations.

articleTitle: Design considerations for the COBRAcable HVDC interconnector
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: TenneT and Energinet.dk - TSO's of the Netherlands and Denmark respectively - are currently in the construction phase of a HVDC cable connection that will interconnect the electricity grids of the two countries. The new interconnector will run between two onshore converter stations; from Eemshaven station in the Netherlands to Endrup station in Denmark [1]. The COBRAcable interconnector links the two AC networks via a HVDC symmetrical monopole configuration connected by submarine and land cables of ±320 kV. Bi-directional power transmission capability is foreseen. The nominal transmission power capacity of the link is 700 MW, as referred to the AC side of the sending end. The reactive power exchange capacity is ±230 MVAr at each end. The COBRAcable project is currently in the detailed design phase and this paper's work was prepared during the development and early stages of the design phase. The work presented here has been part of TSO's overall responsibility task to ensure and check the smooth technical integration of the converters with the cable and of the HVDC system into the AC network. Therefore, certain design aspects were studied in more detail; two of those are presented in this paper: the energization process (in chapter 3) and, ; the HVDC system compatibility with the DC cable (in chapter 4).

articleTitle: Reliability performances of grid-integrated PV systems with varying climatic conditions
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Photovoltaics (PV) power generation is vulnerable to climate changes because operating voltages of PV cells can be affected by the operating temperature, power outputs can be affected by the levels of irradiances, and level of cell current can be affected by shading resulting from various causes. This paper explores variations in climatic conditions, operating temperature, irradiance, and shading on a PV system that sits on an ageing spectrum. Such PV systems are integrated to a power grid and the reliability performances of the grid were assessed using Monet Carlo simulation under varying demand conditions. The study incorporates probabilistic climate change projections from UKCP09 under different emission scenarios low, medium and high, for three time frames 2020s (2010-2039) , 2050s (2040-2069) and 2080s (2070-2099) based on observation of 30 years historical weather data. Case study results suggest that the PV systems are vulnerable to climatic conditions considerably in the long run. The reliability performance of a power system can be affected by high penetration of PV power generation that is susceptible to varying climatic conditions. The impacts resulting from climatic conditions are inconstant with the ageing conditions of PV systems. A quantitative assessment is required for tracing PV system influences on a power system that is susceptible to varying climatic conditions.

articleTitle: Benefits of distributed power generation for voltage support in GB transmission system: Case study on the south-east region
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Distributed Generation (DG) has lately attracted great interest by energy market players due to its potential for independent provision of active and reactive power. High penetration of renewable energy sources can, however, adversely affect the power system. As such, the power system needs to be reinforced or expanded to be able to successfully cope with potential issues. It has been argued, though, that support from DG could form part of the solution as a means of driving down network reinforcement costs. In this context, this work particularly focuses on the potential of DG to support the voltage of the transmission system by providing reactive power when requested to. The south-east region of National Grid's transmission system in Great Britain is used as a case study to demonstrate the benefit from utilisation of DG. The main contribution of this paper is to specifically demonstrate that distributed allocation of reactive power sources can alleviate imminent voltage instability issues, while minimising transmission reinforcement costs.

articleTitle: Fast fault location scheme for distribution systems based on fault transients
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: This paper presents a combined double-end and single-end fault locator for distribution systems. The technique lies under the impedance based category and uses the fault generated high frequency components to locate the faults. The combination of double-end and single-end allows the method to discriminate between faults on the main feeder and those on laterals. Also, the method only requires a short data window as it depends on the high frequency components. The evaluation of the method considers different system and fault parameters e.g. loading taps, loading unbalance, fault type and fault resistance. To validate the proposed technique, the IEEE 34 nodes system is used to simulate different test cases.

articleTitle: Value of load transfer capacity in distribution network design
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: A fundamental review of the philosophy of distribution network operation and design is carried out to inform the industry, consumers, regulator and government, and facilitate a cost effective delivery of the UK Government energy policy objectives. Within the review potential benefit of load transfer capacity used to improve the reliability performance of the system is quantified. This is the subject addressed within this paper, showing used methodology and analysed case studies. The cost-benefit analysis is used to establish the reliability and cost performance of various network designs and emergency operation strategies. Potential benefit of load transfer capacity is calculated for different drivers: network loading, topology, voltage level, construction, and assets failure rate. It is found that the value of LTC is higher in low reliable networks and in systems with higher load. The value of LTC is less sensitive towards the number of supplied substations.

articleTitle: Design of a simplified fuzzy logic power system stabilizer for dynamic reduction of a power system model
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified fuzzy logic power system stabilizer (SFL-PSS) is utilized in a reduced order power system consisting of one synchronous machine with IEEE type-1 excitation and mechanical systems connected to the network through transmission lines. Knowledge of the high bus voltage is employed to change the standard Heffron-Phillips model. Moreover, a reduction technique is applied to reduce the order of the power system and improve the power system stability by adapting the controller's parameters in real time. This is done in order to restrain the distortion caused by any modifications in the operating conditions and the constructions of transmission lines. The results validate the efficiency and stability of the projected SFL-PSS with changed operating conditions and a change of parameters in transmission lines.

articleTitle: Optimal solution to isolate the high impedance/ broken conductor fault in 11 kV overhead line in distribution network
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: This paper deals with the concept development of an adaptive protection system for broken conductor and high impedance faults in 11 kV overhead line distribution network. There are several numbers of 11kV feeders and OHL lines are built due to rapidly growing power demand in Al Ain Distribution Network. The trend in AADC network is to progressively replace / refurbish old substations and equipment with new one. HiZ faults are a great challenge in AADC due to nature of soil in eastern region of Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates. In addition, AADC challenges in existing network include pole fires as difficult to detect by protection system for broken conductor/HiZ fault. Additional operational costs to be estimated by Distribution Companies prior to implementation of measures for preventing / minimizing high impedance faults under the pressure of continual customer satisfaction and regulatory controls. This paper also briefly analysis live line tests which were conducted in 11kV network in AADC. Live line tests were conducted with different types of fault with different vendors in order to analyse performance of available HiZ/BCP relays and evaluate required algorithms to detect HiZ/BCP fault.

Author Keywords: GOOSE — Generic Object Oriented Substation Event

articleTitle: Energy storage planning for resiliency enhancement against renewable energy curtailment
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: The optimal allocation and sizing of energy storage systems in transmission networks for resiliency enhancement against renewable energy curtailment is investigated in this paper. The objective function is defined as total operation and investment costs which should be minimized subject to technical constraints. The impact of ESS in reducing the energy curtailments in normal and contingency situations is analysed. The proposed model is tested on IEEE RTS 24 bus to justify its applicability and strength.

articleTitle: Power system resilience assessment considering of integrated natural gas system
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Power system and natural gas (NG) system are two critical infrastructures (CI) that modern society depends on. The power system designed with conventional reliability criterion can neither effectively anticipate nor respond to high impact, low probability (HILP) events such as earthquake. At the same time, increasingly utilization of NG for electricity generation leads to rising intersystem coupling of power system and NG system. The interdependence imposes power system potential risk, such as failure propagation trigged by gas network contingency. Taken together with power system intrinsic complexity, these factors could operate to amplify disruptive effects. In this context, this paper aims to develop an effective model and approach to assess power system resilience considering associated fuel supply system based on two performance metrics: Expected Demand Not Supplied (EDNS) and Probability of Load Curtailments (PLC). It develops models of NG system, power system and their interdependence for quantitative measurement purpose, and generates an integral simulation frame using non-sequential Monte Carlo simulation. Finally, it conducts case studies on modified Belgian gas transmission system and IEEE-24 reliability test system to justify the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Live line snow and ice coverage detection of ceramic insulator using Gabor image features
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: This study proposes a novel inspection technique for remote information extraction from electrical insulator surface under complex climate condition using image processing. Experiments conducted on recorded images of snow, ice and water covered insulator. Gabor filtering algorithm is utilized for extracting a set of Gabor phase congruency features from insulator images for the presence or absence of snow, ice and water droplets using minimum distance nearest neighbour classifier.

articleTitle: Fragility curve based storm modelling of distribution networks with staff constraints
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Normally reliable distribution systems often are at their most unreliable during storms. High winds can cause significant damage to overhead lines. The high number of faults can block normal paths to reconfigure the network to restore supply to customers meaning that faults can have a significantly higher impact than if they occurred during normal network operation. Unfortunately, the high number of faults means that network operators are unable to repair all faults simultaneously, prioritising those repairs that will benefit the most customers. While many studies have focused on the damage done by a storm, the recovery after a storm is often modelled using high level assumptions around average repair times. This paper details a methodology for estimating the impact of storms on a network with specified staff levels and shows the impact changing staff levels has on network resilience.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of PI and PI-PSO in improving power quality of an autonomous microgrid
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: To achieve optimum quality of power in an autonomous microgrid (MG), a control strategy based on the self-tuning method and synchronous reference frame with PI controller is proposed. In the proposed system, fixed gain values were used for PI controller which are not appropriate for sudden changes in the system i.e. transition of MG to islanding mode, load changes, etc. For tuning of PI controller parameters, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is utilized to get an adaptable operation and to accomplish better power quality. The principal parameters considered here are, regulation of voltage and frequency, steady-state and dynamic response and harmonic distortion, mainly when microgrid is islanded. The performance of PI and PI-PSO is compared in this paper by simulating AC microgrid in MATLAB/Simulink environment. Detailed results of the system are provided in order to authenticate viability of proposed arrangement.

articleTitle: Enhancing distribution network visibility using contingency analysis tools
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: The East Kent area in the South East of England is the good example of how the uptake of distributed generation is changing the way electricity networks operate. This paper identifies the technical and operational challenges facing transmission and distribution networks in the East Kent area. It introduces the Kent Active System Management (KASM) project, which develops an online contingency analysis solution designed to assist UK Power Networks (UKPN) in maximising asset utilisation while maintaining the network security.

articleTitle: A simulation framework to analyse dependent weather-induced faults
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: A framework for simulating weather-induced dependent faults across networks is proposed and demonstrated on a truncated GB network representative of the Scottish and Northern English network. Different weather scenarios are simulated on the test network considering location and wind-speed intensity, analysed using Monte-Carlo simulation. The sensitivity of the network to co-occurrence of faults is simulated by changing the sensitivity of network assets to wind speed via an exponential function. Greater sensitivity to wind speed induces a significant increase in outages, as reflected by risk metrics, specifically Expected Energy Not Served and Expected Maximum Load Shed.

articleTitle: Over current relay coordination in a real system with wind farm integration using hybrid genetic algorithm approach
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Relay Coordination is necessary to ensure the protective relays in the power grid operate as soon as the identification of faults and also to keep the healthy feeders remains not to be tripped. The addition of distributed generations (DG) change the original steady state value, fault current value and direction of current due to their local distribution. The addition of more and more DG sources causes the reduction of sensitivity and selectivity which results in the maloperation of the relays. This paper focuses on the adaptive relay coordination of over current relays in the presence of wind farms. The artificial intelligence method selected is hybrid genetic algorithm approach, and relay coordination is carried out for the different wind speed conditions as well as according to the wind generators (WG) in operation. The test system selected is a real system in South India, and the result is found to be satisfactory.

articleTitle: Simulative analyses of dynamical behaviour of steam-powered turbo generators during power system incidents with a higher rate of change of frequency
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: The national goal in the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland is to cover 40 % of electricity demand by renewable generating plants in 2020. This leads to less inertia in the power system and higher rates of change of frequency (ROCOF) after grid faults. This publication focuses on the dynamic behaviour of electrical generators of five different turbo generators during transients of mains frequency with a higher ROCOF. The results show that different turbo generators react in diverse ways to the frequency excursions used for the studies. The electrical torque leads according to a first estimation to torsional moments and fatigue of material of the shaft line in a tolerable range for single events. An adjustment of controllers optimized for higher ROCOF could reduce occurring oscillations. At least one investigated CCGT could trip due to protection system settings, which urges further studies.

articleTitle: Per-phase controller for medium voltage full-bridge modular multilevel converters
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: This work proposes a per-phase control architecture for a fullbridge modular multilevel converter (FB-MMC) intended for medium voltage applications, such as MVDC multi-terminal distribution networks in off-shore wind farms or MVDC networks in industrial plants. The converter under study operates with 20kV on the DC side and is connected to an 11kV AC grid through a Δ-Y transformer. The response to a single line to ground (SLG) AC fault of the converter controlled with the proposed per-phase control architecture is compared with the conventional MMC using dq control. Simulation results in Matlab-Plecs prove that the proposed control approach has better response to a SLG fault compared with the conventional one, while maintaining a simple structure.

articleTitle: Unconventional flashover mitigation measures to improve the lightning performance of transmission lines
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: In this paper an evaluation of the lightning performance of standard UK 400 kV tower configurations is performed. For the evaluation, various soil resistivities, three tower heights as well as two stroke current distributions, CIGRE and one derived from a lightning location system are taken into account. Furthermore, two flashover mitigation methods, arresters and underbuilt wires are investigated, which are proposed to reduce the back-flashover rate of the line.

articleTitle: Condition monitoring in low voltage circuit breaker technology
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Overheating is the single biggest cause of failure in switchgear. Modern circuit protection is provided by digital overcurrent relays which are operated by current, not heat so abnormal heating caused by loose connection bolts, ventilation failure or worn contacts is usually left undetected by conventional circuit breakers. This can lead to pre-mature failure of switchgear and also constitutes a potential fire hazard. Thermal imaging can help prevent this but is only valid for that `snapshot' in time. Continuous condition monitoring of the temperature of switchgear can substantially minimise down time of the installation and reduce the risk of fire.

articleTitle: Transient testing of communication based distribution automation schemes
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: In order to reduce customer outage minutes overhead distribution networks are equipped with reclosers. Such reclosers, when automated using voltage based logic or communication media, allow feeders to be interconnected to quickly restore power to areas not affected by a fault. Communication based automation schemes allow for a very fast location and isolation of the fault, and restoration is possible in under 400ms. However, such schemes are custom made and require thorough testing prior to installation to test the switching logic at various fault locations, which is usually only achieved in lab environments and requires big effort. Schemes should also be tested during commissioning to verify that the communication networks can handle the traffic once installed. This paper will outline the importance of testing to ensure proper functioning of the installed equipment and will also suggest simple to apply methods for testing of the scheme as a whole using simulated transient faults to mimic real-life conditions as close as possible. In addition examples of tests performed and experience made with tests performed at utilities and manufacturers are shared.

articleTitle: Resilience of power transmission system protection using a new d-q wavelet hybrid technique
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: A new protection system for power transmission lines is presented based on a d-q wavelet hybrid technique (dqWPT). This hybrid technique is developed via the integration of the d-q axis transformation with the wavelet packet transform (WPT). In this proposed method, fault and transient current signals are obtained experimentally. The data compression analysis is carried out using wavelet decomposition and reconstruction based signal processing for the selection of the optimal number of levels of approximations (a) and details (d) for the selected kind of mother wavelets. For optimum choice and faster response of the protection system, the number of levels should be maintained at a minimum level. In order to select the best mother wavelet, the minimum description length (MDL) is used in this paper. The pertinent detailed analyses are briefly summarized in this paper. Sample simulations and measured results of a laboratory transmission line model for various kinds of faults are presented in order to validate the novelty of this new method. Finally, the optimal number of decomposition levels required for transmission line protection system is discussed.

articleTitle: A novel methodology for predicting potential responsiveness in residential demand
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Accurate prediction of available responsive demand guides energy providers and network operators towards potential opportunities for achieving flexible demand response management. This paper proposes a novel methodology in order to estimate the potential of demand responsiveness through shiftable appliances at a residential level. The methodology is based on clustering residential demand profiles into homogenous groups of households using information regarding the willingness of households to participate in demand response, such as their demand profiles and available wet appliances. Three popular clustering algorithms are applied to a set of residential electricity meter readings including K-means, Fuzzy K-means and Dirichlet Process Mixture Model. Moreover, each distinctive group has been characterised in terms of technical and social attributes. Consequently, the potential of demand responsiveness over time for each group of households has been investigated.

articleTitle: Assessment of Al Ain distribution network incidents and lessons learned
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Al Ain Distribution Network is owned, operated and maintained by Al Ain Distribution Company (AADC), an affiliate of ADWEA). It encompass several electrical equipment in over 300 primary substations and around 7500 distribution substations, of voltage levels from 400V to 33kV and spread across 12000 km2 in the Eastern Region of Abu Dhabi Emirate. Governmental initiatives towards achieving excellence for United Arab Emirates require AADC to be in par with top quartile utility performers. Regulatory challenges and customer satisfaction amongst several other factors demand the finest distribution network performance. Outage incidents are common in distribution networks and could happen if assets are aged and safety perspectives are not fully evaluated well in advance. This paper outlines various incidents happened in 3 different types of substations namely 33/11kV Primary Substation NBST-PY, 11/0.4kV Distribution Substation AM-0065, and 33/11kV Package Unit Substation LSMAR-PU in urban area of Al Ain. All of those incidents happened within few days of one week and two of them involved fire. The paper will focus on the lessons learned from the incidents, which will cover impact of such type of incidents on major Key Indexes of the company involving interruption indices such as System Average Interruption Duration Index and Frequency Index (SAIDI&SAIFI) that measure the network performance, continual availability of supply to customer, resources exerted in order to restore supply and repair damages. As customer delight and cost optimisation are main objectives of the company in addition to regulatory compliance, it is critical that such type of incidents and/or impact of their incidents shall be minimised. The paper will aim to assess the correlation between these major incidents, economical effects, incident analysis from technical and managerial prospective, contribution of different users and specialists from operation, maintenance, protection and DMS departmental staff in restoration of the referred incidents and prevention or mitigation of impact of such type of incidents. The incidents happened during low load season also prompted measures that are taken to prepare for any similar incidents and accidents that could occur during summer peak season, to meet the high demand in a secure manner, with low risk of explosion and fire hazard. The incidents also threw light on Business Impact Analysis, which is a prime criterion to prepare Business Continuity plan.

Author Keywords: SAIFI — System Average Interruption Duration Index and Frequency Index

articleTitle: Graph centrality visualisation of power interchange in supergrids — A study of visual analytic challenges for operational control
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: Operational control of the European continental grid with its almost 17,000 nodes, 14,000 transmission lines, 3,900 generation units and a total load of about 400 GW is a precedent example for collaboratively controlling a wide-area transmission system by prevailingly national transmission system operators (TSOs). Due to the free trade of European electricity market and growing integration of renewable sources the power interchange across the interconnection has notably increased. From physical point of view the power interchange is limited due to the capabilities of components in the certain transmission paths (transmission lines, transformers etc.). Especially the tie-line capabilities between the particular control-areas have to be emphasised in this context. The TSOs have to cope with that situation while operating their respective control-areas in safe and secure conditions. This paper describes an approach to give all involved TSOs a plain near-time visualisation of the overall power interchange situation in the entire interconnected grid, including a visual expression of highly affected or participating control-areas respectively. The proposed method is based on a clustergraph model of the interconnected grid and application of centrality measures from graph theory. Furthermore, this approach is a visual analytic concept for approaching the problem of interchange monitoring by means of already available datasets.

articleTitle: The conceptual framework of resilience and its measurement approaches in electrical power systems
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: The resilience assessment of complex and large-scale systems such as electrical power systems has becoming an inseparable part in analysing the reliable performance of the systems in the presence of high-impact, low-probability (HILP) incidents, such as extreme natural disasters. Considering the application of the resilience in various domains, the different definitions can be found for assessment of resilience in one system and several approaches can be applied to measure it. The necessity of increasing the resilience of power system infrastructures in response to HILP disasters for supplying at least emergency loads when facing unexpected and catastrophic events has becoming more and more clear. Reliability evaluation of power systems provides the likely behaviour of a system in normal condition but fails to model the high order contingencies which have low probabilities of occurrence. However, withstanding, absorbing and rapidly recovering from HILP events still remains a significant challenge which can be analysed in resilience assessment. This paper presents a conceptual framework of resilience domains and its measurement approaches, especially a thorough conceptual framework of resilience as a subcategory of vulnerability in electrical power systems. The conceptual difference between resilience and other indices of power system assessment such as reliability, risk and security are also presented in this research.

articleTitle: Distribution system development policy: Resilience and rapid industrial development in Ireland
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Resilience of Transmission and Distribution Networks (RTDN 2017)
abstract: A sustainable relationship between customer expectation, and system development and operation is fundamental to resilience of the distribution system. In its 2014 evidence to the House of Lords on Resilience of Electricity Infrastructure, the IET states “resilience...results from the inter-play of all the multiple inter-related components and factors that form the whole electricity system”. This encapsulates the challenge facing ESB Networks, the Irish DSO, managing an increase in industrial high demand customers, (>40MVA), clustered particularly in the greater Dublin area. The industries dominating this development, including data centre, IT and pharmaceutical industries, are predicated on an expectation of high electricity supply resilience, and typically seek rapid delivery of new facilities as a prerequisite of investment. The corollary of this rapid development in a relatively small geographical region is that the redundancy and capacity which afford resilience to the distribution system are being eroded at a higher rate than conventional distribution system development policies can build to mitigate. The delivery of a social electricity infrastructure which meets these demands while retaining the operational functionality to meet existing customers' expectation requires a detailed understanding of the value customers place on resilience and how this can be matched to the facilities and resources available for grid development and operation. This paper (1) illustrates the existing challenge using power system monitoring and planning data, (2) mathematically describes its technico-economic interaction with system management today, and (3) explores how contemporary concepts applied in planning and services may address these challenges.
